post_conditions.descr: Samtec SSQ-124-02-G-S-RA expansion header: 1 x 24 = 24 contacts, .100 in / 2.54 mm pitch, FEMALE .025 in square-post socket strip, RIGHT-ANGLE (horizontal) entry, through-hole, gold. ADOPTED AT FBV2-EXP-002 (D-237), superseding the Samtec BCS-112-S-D-HE 2 x 12. Configuration per the Samtec SSW/SSQ through-hole datasheet, verified 2026-08-24: SSQ = square tail; 124 = 24 positions per row (the series offers 01 thru 50); 02 = standard-insertion-force lead style, which for a single-row right-angle part sets B = 2.54 mm socket-axis height above the PCB; G = 20 uin gold on contact; S = SINGLE ROW; RA = right angle, which the datasheet lists as available with the -S row option. BODY LENGTH = positions x 2.54 + 0.51 = 61.47 mm; pin 1 to pin 24 span = 23 x 2.54 = 58.42 mm; insulator overhangs the end contact by 1.525 mm at each end - THAT OVERHANG IS WHY TWO 1x12 BODIES CANNOT BE BUTTED INTO A CONTINUOUS 24-POSITION GRID (they would sit 3.050 mm apart against a 2.540 mm pitch). Mates .025 in (0.635 mm) SQUARE POST - the ordinary male header / Dupont standard. 6.3 A per pin with 2 pins powered, 465 VAC / 655 VDC, -55 to +125 C with gold, insertion depth 3.68 to 6.35 mm, 100 mating cycles at 10 uin Au. Hole pattern Ø1.02 mm on 2.54 mm, taken from the Sullins 1-row right-angle recommended PCB layout (drawing 10493, xPxCxx1LGBN-RC) which dimensions the same interface: Ø.040 in [1.02] hole, .100 in [2.54] pitch, tail .024 x .016 in [0.60 x 0.40], tail 3.15 mm below board, body 8.50 mm tall, and 6.53 mm from the tail row to the mating face - THE 6.53 mm IS THE DIMENSION THE WHOLE RIGHT-WALL FIT TURNS ON. LOCAL FRAME: pads run along +X with pin 1 at -29.21; the MATING FACE POINTS ALONG -Y. On the AQROOT board it is placed at rotation 270 so the pins run down the right wall with pin 1 at the top and the mating face pointing at the enclosure recess. THE ENCLOSURE SUPPLIES SHIFT PROTECTION (D-240): a closed-end recess 62.5 mm long against a 60.96 mm male body leaves 1.54 mm of play - 60 percent of one pitch - so a one-position lateral shift is physically impossible. There is no electrical key contact and no proprietary shroud.
